temp.method: Use the published change in average temperature across Earth's land and ocean surface. Keep the comparison period, area covered and status of recent estimates. A satellite measurement of one layer of air is a different measure.
temp.uncertainty: Different datasets cover different places and adjust observations in different ways. Sea-temperature methods and the chosen comparison period also affect results. Recent values may be revised.
temp.boundary: If the source stops updating, show the last reviewed yearly value and say how old it is. Missing months cannot be worked out from a TULIP score.

methane.method: Add the mass of methane released within the source's stated coverage. Keep fossil-fuel, farming, waste, fire and natural sources separate. Estimates from atmospheric measurements and estimates built from individual activities use different methods.
methane.uncertainty: Totals depend on activity records, assumed release rates and how well unusually large leaks and wetlands are measured. Winds and revisions can change how emissions are assigned to sources.
methane.boundary: A rise in methane concentration is not the same as the amount people emitted. Natural releases and the methane removed from the air must also be accounted for.

deforestation.method: Compare forest clearing and yearly changes in forest area with a fixed reference suited to the source. Keep the mapped area and any source warnings attached to the result.
deforestation.uncertainty: Incomplete observations, sampling choices and models affect the estimate. Revisions and the area covered matter too. Missing observations do not mean zero change.
deforestation.boundary: If fresh data are unavailable, keep the last reviewed value and clearly show that it is old. Do not change the score to fill the gap.

industry_farming.method: Compare the farming inputs used with a fixed reference suited to the source. Keep the area covered and any warnings so changes in coverage are not mistaken for changes in farming.
industry_farming.uncertainty: Incomplete observations, sampling choices and models affect the estimate. Revisions and the area covered matter too. Missing observations do not mean zero use.
industry_farming.boundary: If fresh data are unavailable, keep the last reviewed value and clearly show that it is old. Do not change the score to fill the gap.

food.method: Start with production, add imports and subtract exports and additions to stored stocks. Keep food, animal feed, seed, processing and losses separate within each crop or product account.
food.uncertainty: Unrecorded trade, changes in stocks and estimates of feed or waste can change the result. Converting between products and later statistical revisions also adds uncertainty.
food.boundary: Available supply is not the same as the amount people eat. Do not add products measured on incompatible weight bases.

urbanization.method: Use one consistent version of the Global Human Settlement Layer maps to identify built-up land. Compare matching periods and boundaries, keeping population, density and redevelopment information alongside the area change.
urbanization.uncertainty: Map detail, clouds and classification errors affect estimates. Tall buildings, informal settlements and time between observations can also change what the map captures.
urbanization.boundary: Expanding an administrative boundary does not mean new land was built on. Different map versions must be made comparable before measuring change.

migration.method: Record the event, place, hazard and estimated movements, along with the source and confidence. Keep new movements separate from the number of people still displaced. One person moving several times must not be counted as several unique people.

migration.boundary: Not all migration is caused by climate. Do not add new movements to the number of people already displaced as if they were the same kind of count.

resource_depletion.method: Keep two UN measures separate: materials used to meet a country's demand, including production abroad, and materials used within its own economy. Keep totals and amounts per person for each material group. Do not add a total to the parts already inside it.
resource_depletion.uncertainty: The estimates depend on trade models, conversion factors, unrecorded extraction and changes in stocks. Population estimates affect amounts per person, and modelled values may be revised.
resource_depletion.boundary: Material use does not measure remaining reserves, scarcity or the quality of ore. It is also different from extraction alone or recycled content. Missing areas and material groups must not be counted as zero.

carbon_emission.boundary: Keep the last reviewed emissions inventory and show its reporting delay. Concentration in the air and graph influence cannot be converted directly into tonnes emitted.

personal_conveyance.boundary: A journey count alone cannot tell us fuel use, emissions, delay or exposure. Each needs its own supporting activity data.

environ_anomalies.method: For this pilot, compare daily maximum air temperature at 2 metres and corrected daily rainfall with local 1991–2020 values. Count days in the chosen year when both exceed the level reached on only 5% of reference days. Keep both readings, location, time standard and missing-data checks.
environ_anomalies.uncertainty: Station coverage, modelled weather estimates, thresholds and the area combined can change the count. Events close together may also be related rather than independent.
environ_anomalies.boundary: This counts one specific combination of heat and heavy rain, not every combined climate hazard. Do not count a day if either reading is missing or the events fall outside the chosen time window.

el_nino.boundary: When updates are missing, retain the last reviewed value and show its age and source gap. Do not change the score to fill the gap.

amoc.boundary: A local series does not represent the whole ocean. Do not combine readings from incompatible depths, different variables or different reference periods.

wet_bulb_heat.method: Use NASA POWER's hourly wet-bulb temperature for the chosen location and UTC year. Keep the maximum, the level exceeded in the hottest 5% of hours, and hours reaching 26, 28, 30, 32 and 35°C separately. This measure combines heat and humidity. It differs from workplace heat indices, indoor conditions and an individual's exposure.
wet_bulb_heat.uncertainty: Temperature and humidity errors, the size of the mapped area and chosen thresholds affect interpretation. Wind and sunshine matter for other heat indices, while housing and adjustment to local heat affect personal risk.
wet_bulb_heat.boundary: Do not combine daily temperature and humidity extremes from different places or times to calculate this value. Ordinary air temperature is not wet-bulb temperature.

monsoon_volatility.method: Apply only the rainfall part of India's Kerala monsoon-onset rule. After 10 May, at least 60% of the 14 named locations must receive 2.5 millimetres a day for two days in a row. Compare the second day with 1991–2020, and separately compare June–September rainfall averaged across the locations with the same reference period.
monsoon_volatility.uncertainty: These NASA POWER estimates come from a weather grid, not India's official station network. Grid location, rainfall bias, missing readings, terrain and the way locations are averaged can affect the result.
monsoon_volatility.boundary: This rainfall-only check is not the official onset date. Withhold the result if fewer than 27 reference years are usable or any location has an incomplete observation season. Missing rain must not be counted as zero.

permafrost_thaw.method: Keep the site, method, greatest thaw depth and ground temperatures at each depth. Snow, plants and soil conditions help explain the reading. Compare only sites measured in consistent ways.
permafrost_thaw.uncertainty: Northern monitoring sites are sparse and local conditions vary. Sinking ground, snow, moisture, vegetation and sensor depth can all affect the apparent trend.
permafrost_thaw.boundary: One borehole does not measure a region's thawed area or carbon release. The layer that thaws each summer is different from ground that stays unfrozen year-round.

rain_on_snow_flood_risk.method: Keep the river basin, event threshold and the snow, rain, temperature and soil conditions. Identify the forecast model used to estimate the resulting flood risk.
rain_on_snow_flood_risk.uncertainty: River-channel conditions, forecast error and the people or buildings exposed all affect the risk.
rain_on_snow_flood_risk.boundary: Rain falling on snow does not prove that a flood occurred.

peak_glacier_runoff_passage.method: Use comparable long-term records of glaciers, snow, rain and river flow. They must distinguish a temporary rise in meltwater from a lasting decline after the basin's maximum glacier contribution.
peak_glacier_runoff_passage.uncertainty: The timing differs with glacier size and height, rainfall patterns, groundwater storage and the quality of monitoring.
peak_glacier_runoff_passage.boundary: Keep the last reviewed basin finding and show when its evidence is old. Global temperature alone cannot show that a basin has passed this point.

marine_pathogen_range_expansion.boundary: Do not claim a change in geographic range without both environmental coverage and a traceable disease-reporting source.

tropical_cyclone_rapid_intensification.boundary: If new readings are unavailable, keep the last reviewed value and show its age and missing coverage. Do not change the score to fill the gap.

drought_persistence.method: Use the source's six-month rainfall index with a fixed 1991–2020 reference period. Count months at or below −1.0 as meteorological drought and group consecutive months. Report the longest run, total drought months and combined index shortfall separately.
drought_persistence.uncertainty: The rainfall model, statistical fit, reference period, grid location and threshold can change which months qualify. A calendar-year window can split a longer event.
drought_persistence.boundary: Require all twelve monthly values before publishing an event. Missing months are not drought-free. Clearly mark events cut off at a year boundary.

ice_sheet_mass_loss.method: Use the published combination of satellite gravity, surface-height and ice-flow estimates. Keep the method, basin, time period and the way shared measurement errors are handled. State whether positive values mean ice gain or loss.
ice_sheet_mass_loss.uncertainty: Slow land movement after past ice loss, snow compaction and assumed density affect the result. Satellite processing, sparse snowfall records and shared errors between methods also matter.
ice_sheet_mass_loss.boundary: Do not mix glacier totals with ice-sheet totals. Different time periods can be combined only if uncertainty and shared errors are handled explicitly.

sea_ice_season_loss.method: Keep the ocean region, season, satellite or buoy dataset and reference period with the ice-season measure.
sea_ice_season_loss.uncertainty: Winds and natural climate variability can change regional results from one year to the next.
sea_ice_season_loss.boundary: An Arctic-wide change does not show how far ice retreated at a particular location.

coastal_inundation_risk.method: Use NOAA's daily high-tide flooding records for one named gauge, a fixed height reference and calendar year. Count minor, moderate and major threshold crossings separately. Keep the maximum level, time, missing readings and the station's threshold definitions.
coastal_inundation_risk.uncertainty: Land movement, height references, gaps in gauge data, waves and storms affect readings. Flood defences and the accuracy of land-height maps affect how those readings relate to nearby places.

arctic_shipping_expansion.method: Combine checked ship-position messages inside a defined Arctic area. Keep vessel type, flag, route and reception coverage, and remove repeated messages before counting activity.
arctic_shipping_expansion.uncertainty: Not all vessels must carry tracking equipment, and some signals are missed. Identity changes, route boundaries and missing small boats can affect counts.
arctic_shipping_expansion.boundary: Missing tracking coverage does not mean no ships. Keep the last comparable period and state the coverage limits.

ocean_acidification.method: Check seawater-chemistry readings before estimating acidity or how easily shells can form. Keep temperature, salt content, pressure, depth, instruments and the equations used with the result.

pacific_decadal_oscillation.boundary: Missing periods are unknown, not neutral conditions. Do not mix different index definitions or treat a TULIP score as an observed climate reading.

coastal_hypoxia.method: Use NOAA's reported area of low-oxygen water, converted to square kilometres for display. Keep the survey dates, Gulf survey area and bottom-water oxygen threshold attached.
coastal_hypoxia.uncertainty: NOAA's yearly status value has no published uncertainty interval. Survey timing and spacing, storms, mixing, river flow and nutrient inputs can change the mapped area.
coastal_hypoxia.boundary: Keep the last validated survey and show its age. Reject records missing a clear year, area, threshold or survey window. An unobserved year is not zero, and the Gulf result does not represent another coast.

marine_food_web_simplification.method: Group verified species records only where area, depth, season and sampling period are comparable. Keep the number of records and the contributing datasets visible.
marine_food_web_simplification.uncertainty: Species records support investigation but do not directly measure the structure of a food web.
marine_food_web_simplification.boundary: Show insufficient coverage when records are inadequate. Do not invent the number of species in unsurveyed areas.

pelagic_species_redistribution.method: Check species-location records and keep how they were sampled. Compare each species' average location across similar multi-year periods.
pelagic_species_redistribution.uncertainty: Records of where a species was found may omit where people looked without finding it. Uneven survey effort can look like movement even when the species has not shifted.
pelagic_species_redistribution.boundary: Do not publish a trend without enough coverage across both time and space.

peat_oxidation_pulse.method: Keep drained organic-soil area separate from estimated total carbon dioxide emissions. Calculate emissions per hectare only when area and emissions cover the same place, year, category and data release.
peat_oxidation_pulse.uncertainty: FAOSTAT uses mapped area and standard emission rates. Peat-soil maps, land-cover classes, climate assumptions, country reports and revisions affect the estimate.
peat_oxidation_pulse.boundary: This does not measure all wetlands, newly drained area, fire emissions or the flow from one project. Do not divide by missing or zero area, or add countries to regional totals that already include them.

ocean_carbon_uptake_weakening.method: Compare the ocean's carbon uptake and uptake efficiency with a fixed reference suited to the source. Keep the area covered and any source warnings with the result.
ocean_carbon_uptake_weakening.uncertainty: Sparse measurements, model limits, revisions and geographic coverage can change the estimate. Missing observations do not mean no uptake.
ocean_carbon_uptake_weakening.boundary: Keep the last reviewed value when updates stop and show its age and coverage gap. Do not change scores to fill missing observations.

madden_julian_oscillation.method: Use NOAA's daily ROMI record, retaining both components that locate the pattern and the source's measure of its strength. ROMI is a particular tracking method and must not be relabelled as the different RMM index.
madden_julian_oscillation.uncertainty: Results depend on satellite estimates of outgoing heat, smoothing over 9 days, removal of a 40-day background and patterns defined over 30–96 days. Recent observations may be revised.
madden_julian_oscillation.boundary: Keep the last validated daily record and flag it as old after ten days. Do not invent missing components or substitute a different index. Strength alone does not establish effects on regional rainfall.

humidity_amplification.method: Use NASA POWER's daily amount of water vapour through the whole air column. Multiply centimetres of water equivalent by 10 to obtain kilograms per square metre. Compare each complete year's average with the average for 1991–2020, keeping coverage and location clear.
humidity_amplification.uncertainty: The estimate comes from a weather grid. Inputs, grid location, later corrections, the height of the air column and yearly averaging can affect the comparison.
humidity_amplification.boundary: Require at least 95% valid daily coverage. Otherwise keep the last validated complete year and show its age. Relative humidity is a different measure, and an increase alone does not prove warming caused it.

atmospheric_dryness.method: Pair hourly air temperature and relative humidity for the same location and UTC time. Calculate how much more water vapour the air could hold at that temperature. Keep the average, maximum, 95th percentile and counts above stated thresholds.
atmospheric_dryness.uncertainty: The estimate uses gridded weather data and a nonlinear formula, so temperature or humidity errors can grow during calculation. A yearly outdoor pattern is not the exposure at a particular leaf.
atmospheric_dryness.boundary: Require at least 95% of hourly pairs to be complete. Otherwise retain the last validated complete year and show its age. Missing hours do not mean no drying pressure.

ozone_formation_pressure.method: Match ozone readings with the gases that form it and with temperature, sunlight, winds and air mixing at the same times. Keep monitor locations, local emissions and pollution carried in from elsewhere clear.
ozone_formation_pressure.uncertainty: Chemical reactions are not simple one-to-one relationships. Natural emissions, imported pollution, clouds, still air, monitor coverage and mixing can affect which causes are responsible.
ozone_formation_pressure.boundary: Do not blame an ozone event on heat, freight or one gas alone without matching chemical and weather observations.

smoke_exposure_burden.method: Keep the definition of illness or death, exposure model, time delay and population covered. Identify any adjustment for age and the comparison used to estimate the effect. Counts, rates and shares attributed to exposure are separate measures.
smoke_exposure_burden.uncertainty: Missed cases, coding errors, exposure estimates and delayed effects affect results. Other causes, model choices and population counts also matter.
smoke_exposure_burden.boundary: Exposure to a hazard does not by itself establish illness or deaths. Different case definitions must not be combined.

agricultural_labor_exposure.method: Keep the definition of illness or death, exposure model, time delay and population covered. Identify any adjustment for age and the comparison used to estimate the effect. Counts, rates and shares attributed to exposure are separate measures.
