grid_peak_load_stress.method: Compare hourly electricity demand and the previous day's forecast for the same power-system area. Report peak demand, the level exceeded in 5% of hours, data completeness and the average size of forecast errors.
grid_peak_load_stress.uncertainty: Area boundaries, on-site generation, programmes that shift demand, power transfers and missing hours can change the signal. Forecasts may also be revised.
grid_peak_load_stress.boundary: Demand alone does not show spare generation, emergency reserves or a breach of reliability standards. Withhold results when hourly coverage or matched forecasts are insufficient.

battery_supply_chain_pressure.method: Keep battery demand, factory capacity, actual production, mineral needs and battery chemistry separate. Compare market shares only within the same supply-chain stage and year.
battery_supply_chain_pressure.uncertainty: Battery-size estimates, vehicle sales, storage uses, private market data and stockpiling affect demand estimates. Ownership, trade, changing chemistry and revisions also matter.
battery_supply_chain_pressure.boundary: Announced factories are not operating supply, and capacity is not actual production. Future projections are not current readings, and global market shares do not show impacts at an individual mine.

biodiversity_intactness_loss.method: Remove repeated species records and invalid locations. Group the remaining records by species, period and equal-sized map area, keeping the amount of sampling clear.
biodiversity_intactness_loss.uncertainty: More records can reflect more observers or more data being published, not necessarily more wildlife.
biodiversity_intactness_loss.boundary: Keep the previous reviewed dataset if updates fail and show its age. Missing online records do not mean zero species.

wildfire_regime_shift.method: Add the mapped burned area in forests, savannas, shrubland, grassland and other non-crop areas, keeping cropland separate. Compare years with 2003–2022. Also find the shortest run of months, allowing for a year boundary, containing at least 90% of that year's non-crop burned area.
wildfire_regime_shift.uncertainty: The 500-metre maps can miss small fires or cloudy periods. Land-cover labels, boundaries, managed burning, monthly timing and revisions affect the result.
wildfire_regime_shift.boundary: Reject incomplete country-year coverage. Hotspot counts are not hectares burned, mapped burning is not always wildfire, and area alone does not measure ecological damage.

freshwater_ecosystem_collapse.method: Use the US river and stream survey for 2018–2019, with its weights for representing unsampled waters. Keep fish and bottom-dwelling animal indicators separate, including good, fair, poor and unassessed categories, estimated river lengths and confidence limits.
freshwater_ecosystem_collapse.uncertainty: Site access, sampling weights, reference conditions and regional calibration affect estimates. Missing fish samples and changes in survey design can also matter.
freshwater_ecosystem_collapse.boundary: Require complete categories, confidence limits, geography and indicator records. This survey covers the contiguous United States' rivers and streams. It cannot establish the condition of one waterbody, lakes, global freshwater or ecosystem collapse.

crop_yield_volatility.method: Divide harvested production by harvested area for each crop. Remove the longer-term trend over a fixed stated period before comparing yearly departures or relative variability. Keep crops with different units separate.
crop_yield_volatility.uncertainty: Revised production or area estimates, several growing seasons, informal production and the way the trend is removed can change variability.
crop_yield_volatility.boundary: Variable harvests do not prove a climate cause. Weather, farming methods, prices, conflict and pests need to be considered separately.

farm_heat_stress.method: Convert the source's thousands of hours to hours by multiplying by exactly 1,000. Keep its assumptions of 400 watts of physical work and sun exposure, along with employed population, year, place and model version.
farm_heat_stress.uncertainty: The source provides modelled estimates without an uncertainty interval for each observation. Weather inputs, formal-job coverage, job allocation, work intensity, breaks and adjustment to heat affect the result.
farm_heat_stress.boundary: Keep the last validated release and show its age. Estimated lost working capacity is not measured absence, injury or lost wages, and it does not cover all informal farm work.

fertilizer_price_shock.method: Use the source's global fertiliser price index in current US dollars, with 2010 set to 100. Calculate changes over one, three and twelve months only when the matching consecutive months are present.
fertilizer_price_shock.uncertainty: The source gives no uncertainty interval for each month. The products included, their weights, exchange and dollar conditions, estimates and revisions affect comparisons.
fertilizer_price_shock.boundary: Keep the last validated series and show its age. Reject missing months or changed source layouts. The global index alone does not show a local farmer's prices, affordability, harvest loss or food-price effects.

food_import_exposure.method: Divide net imports by domestic supply for the stated group of foods, using its defined weights or calorie conversion. Keep negative results, stocks, re-exports and food aid visible.
food_import_exposure.uncertainty: Unrecorded trade, stocks, re-exports, calorie conversions and delayed reports can change the estimated dependence on imports.
food_import_exposure.boundary: Different foods cannot be added by weight without a stated conversion. Missing trade records do not mean zero imports.

vector_borne_disease_expansion.method: Keep each disease measure separate. For dengue, retain the model's climate-based estimate of transmission potential for each mosquito species. For malaria, retain the length of the season suitable for transmission for each parasite. Keep the place, year, units and method clear.
vector_borne_disease_expansion.uncertainty: These are modelled estimates without an interval for each observation. Weather inputs, model thresholds and missing factors such as immunity, control measures or health-care access affect interpretation.
vector_borne_disease_expansion.boundary: Keep the last validated release and show its age. Suitable climate does not prove actual infections, disease rates or occupation of a new area. Do not combine the different disease measures into one number.

critical_infrastructure_fragility.method: For qualifying US DOE-417 electricity incidents, multiply reported customers affected by event duration only when both are available. Keep the utility, area, disturbance type, power lost and missing-duration coverage with each record.
critical_infrastructure_fragility.uncertainty: Customer counts can be preliminary and restoration may happen in stages. Reports cover major qualifying incidents rather than every outage. Overlaps, local time conventions and missing durations affect the total.
critical_infrastructure_fragility.boundary: Withhold customer-hours if either input is missing. Reject empty or changed tables. These electricity reports do not establish the condition of water, transport, health or communications systems.

disaster_recovery_inequality.method: Within each selected disaster declaration, compare the share of valid applicants eligible for FEMA's Individuals and Households Program and the award per eligible applicant. Measure the gap between the highest and lowest qualifying city-ZIP groups. Require at least three groups, including two with eligible applicants.
disaster_recovery_inequality.uncertainty: These are aggregated administrative records. Differences can reflect damage, housing tenure, eligibility, paperwork, application rates, timing and local prices rather than unequal treatment or recovery speed.
disaster_recovery_inequality.boundary: Require at least six qualifying declarations and complete, valid records without duplicate IDs. Missing places do not mean zero assistance. These data alone cannot establish demographic discrimination, unmet household needs or how fully people recovered.

talik_expansion.method: Keep the site, depth, measuring method and monitoring period with records of ground that remains unfrozen.
talik_expansion.uncertainty: Some unfrozen zones are temporary and may freeze again.
talik_expansion.boundary: One unfrozen zone does not establish loss of frozen ground across a region.

pollinator_colony_collapse.method: Identify the species or type of colony, survey method, amount of survey effort and season. Keep confirmed causes separate from suspected causes.
pollinator_colony_collapse.uncertainty: Apparent declines may reflect changes in detection, management or migration rather than population loss alone.
pollinator_colony_collapse.boundary: Not every decline in pollinating insects is colony collapse.

tropospheric_ozone.method: Keep monitor methods, quality checks, averaging time, weather and area covered. Distinguish observations from modelled values and calculate exposure only using the named method.
tropospheric_ozone.uncertainty: Monitor location, air mixing, transported pollution, clouds, temperature, chemical reactions and missing hours affect the estimate.
tropospheric_ozone.boundary: Temperature or emissions of ozone-forming gases alone do not measure ozone concentration. Ground-level and upper-atmosphere ozone are different and must remain separate.

marine_heatwaves.method: Compare daily sea-surface temperature with a fixed reference and the source's threshold for each season. Keep event duration, greatest temperature excess, accumulated excess and area separate, including the rules for missing days.
marine_heatwaves.uncertainty: Clouds, ice, coastal map cells, satellite processing, reference-period length and heat below the surface can affect event estimates.
marine_heatwaves.boundary: Do not bridge longer data gaps than the method allows. Heat exposure alone does not prove ecosystem damage.

fracking_wastewater_lakes.method: Keep the facility, route the wastewater could take, volume, chemical contents, receiving water and current status clear.
fracking_wastewater_lakes.uncertainty: Reporting quality and the ways people or ecosystems could be exposed differ by site.
fracking_wastewater_lakes.boundary: Oil or gas production alone does not prove that wastewater was released or water contaminated.

cattle_grazing_overcompaction.method: Compare soil measurements at stated depths and moisture levels with a suitable reference area. Keep soil type, grazing history and instrument method clear.
cattle_grazing_overcompaction.uncertainty: Natural differences in soil and changes in seasonal moisture can affect the measurements.
cattle_grazing_overcompaction.boundary: Grazing alone does not prove harmful soil compaction. Soil measurements or specific supporting evidence are needed.

nitrous_oxide.method: Add only non-overlapping EDGAR nitrous-oxide source categories for the same country and year. Keep category records, gas identity, unit conversions and inventory version. Atmospheric concentration remains separate background information.
nitrous_oxide.uncertainty: Activity records, nitrogen inputs, emission factors, soil and climate differences, industrial categories and revisions affect totals. Source records do not provide a numerical interval for each observation.
nitrous_oxide.boundary: Concentration in air does not establish a source's emissions. Do not double-count categories or convert CO₂-equivalent to gas mass without the stated warming factor. Missing rows are not zero.

antarctic_shelf_instability.method: Review satellite height, gravity, ice-speed, grounding-boundary and ocean records for each named Antarctic sector. Different shelf processes must not be combined into a single continent-wide threshold.
antarctic_shelf_instability.uncertainty: There are few observations beneath ice shelves, and the points at which instability develops are deeply uncertain. Ice loss alone does not identify its cause.
antarctic_shelf_instability.boundary: Keep the last reviewed regional assessment and show its age. A global sea-level trend cannot establish that a particular shelf is unstable.

topsoil_salinization_fields.method: Use field salt measurements or checked maps alongside irrigation-water quality, drainage, groundwater depth and crop information. Keep currently affected area, yearly land loss and crop-loss costs separate.
topsoil_salinization_fields.uncertainty: Salt levels vary within fields. Soil type, moisture, sensor accuracy, naturally salty ground and older estimates of annual losses affect interpretation.
topsoil_salinization_fields.boundary: Show missing surveys and the age of the last validated map. Drought alone does not measure soil salt. Not all salinity is human-caused, and land at risk is not necessarily already affected.

staple_food_price_volatility.method: Use a defined set of basic foods and prices adjusted for inflation. Compare similar markets and retain information about household spending, supply shocks and policy changes.
staple_food_price_volatility.uncertainty: Exchange rates, market selection, subsidies, missing reports and product quality can move prices independently of physical supply.
staple_food_price_volatility.boundary: Do not publish a trend from market records that are too sparse or not comparable.

sulfur_dioxide.method: Keep the amount emitted separate from the concentration measured in outdoor air. Identify sources, monitors, fuel sulfur, pollution controls and methods.
sulfur_dioxide.uncertainty: Outdoor readings combine several sources with air movement, chemical reactions and removal onto surfaces.
sulfur_dioxide.boundary: A concentration reading cannot identify a sector's contribution without evidence separating the sources.

coral_bleaching.method: Keep coral species, survey method, depth, heat measure and exposure duration clear. Local water quality helps explain the response.
coral_bleaching.uncertainty: Satellite heat estimates need checks against observations on reefs. Sensitivity differs by species, prior adjustment, depth and other stresses.
coral_bleaching.boundary: A warm reading alone does not establish bleaching. Duration, reef location and field evidence or a validated heat-stress method are needed.

invasive_species_encroachment.method: Match an approved list of non-native species to checked GBIF location records. Compare the map cells where they are recorded with a fixed reference period.
invasive_species_encroachment.uncertainty: Species names and classifications change, while reporting and survey effort are uneven.
invasive_species_encroachment.boundary: Keep the previous reviewed value if updates fail, and show the age and coverage of the source.

deepwater_petroleum_spill_risk.method: Identify the offshore facility, possible release route, estimated volume status, response plan and investigation status.
deepwater_petroleum_spill_risk.uncertainty: A risk estimate describes a possibility. It does not predict that a spill will occur.
deepwater_petroleum_spill_risk.boundary: Do not present the risk of a release as a confirmed spill.

volatile_organic_compounds.method: Identify each organic gas and keep the sampling method, duration, detection limit and quality checks. Different compounds can be added only on an explicitly stated weight or chemical-reactivity basis.
volatile_organic_compounds.uncertainty: Some gases evaporate or are lost during sampling more readily than others. Detection limits, sharp local differences and rapid chemical reactions affect readings.
volatile_organic_compounds.boundary: An odour, total hydrocarbon reading or unspecified organic-gas signal does not establish the concentration of a particular compound.

soil_microbial_depletion.method: Keep soil depth, moisture, season, laboratory method, sample storage and reference condition clear.
soil_microbial_depletion.uncertainty: Different methods measure different properties of microbes, and activity changes with the season.
soil_microbial_depletion.boundary: Crop yield or soil organic matter alone does not establish a loss of microbes.

surface_water_storage_instability.method: Identify the waterbody and how its stored volume is measured. Keep the reference and observation periods, inflows, outflows and exchanges with groundwater clear, including the total used in any percentage.
surface_water_storage_instability.uncertainty: Seasonal changes, satellite limits, basin boundaries and missing data restrict what can be concluded.
surface_water_storage_instability.boundary: One lake does not describe regional water security. Unassessed basins must not be classified as stable.

pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.method: Identify the pesticide and its breakdown products. Keep sediment properties, animal species and tissue, size, fat content, diet level, sampling method and detection limits. State whether concentrations use wet or dry weight, and retain water readings and contamination history.
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.uncertainty: Build-up differs by chemical, species, tissue, diet, season and how the body processes it. Accumulation within an organism is different from increasing concentration up a food chain.
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.boundary: One animal cannot establish increasing contamination up a food chain. Do not mix chemicals or wet- and dry-weight readings. Sediment detection is not a tissue dose, and not every pesticide persists or accumulates.

anoxic_dead_zones.method: Keep the station, depth, measuring method, tide, season and uncertainty with each oxygen reading.
anoxic_dead_zones.uncertainty: Low oxygen has natural and local causes. Depth and timing are essential for interpreting a reading.
anoxic_dead_zones.boundary: Nutrients, algae or separated water layers alone do not prove persistent low oxygen.

ice_albedo_feedback_loops.method: Compare how much sunlight snow or sea ice reflects with a fixed seasonal reference. Keep cloud, melt-pond and sensor uncertainty clear instead of assigning every reflectivity change the same warming effect.
ice_albedo_feedback_loops.uncertainty: Clouds, melt ponds, snow-grain size, airborne particles and surface type change the strength of the effect.
ice_albedo_feedback_loops.boundary: Keep the prior reviewed seasonal result when observations are missing, and show gaps or changes in satellite processing.

forest_dieback_areas.method: Keep forest type, tree species, the method used to identify deaths, reference period and whether causes are confirmed.
forest_dieback_areas.uncertainty: A change in tree cover seen from above may reflect harvesting, fire or normal seasonal changes.
forest_dieback_areas.boundary: Do not call a loss of visible tree cover forest die-off without evidence that trees died within a defined area.

combined_sewer_overflow.method: Identify the discharge outlet, rainfall, receiving water, duration, volume and treatment status. Keep the way overflow was measured or estimated.
combined_sewer_overflow.uncertainty: Volume and duration may be estimates. Monitoring coverage and how the overflow is linked to rain differ between systems.
combined_sewer_overflow.boundary: Urban rain alone does not prove a sewage overflow. There must be a combined rainwater-sewage system and evidence of overflow or water flows exceeding its capacity.

humanitarian_resource_gaps.method: For each aid plan, subtract received funding linked to that plan from its current revised financial requirement. Report a shortfall of zero if funding is higher. Keep original requirements, revisions, pledges, locations and reporting year separate.
humanitarian_resource_gaps.uncertainty: This measures reported missing money, not every gap in staff, supplies, access or delivered aid. Delayed reports, unlinked funds, exchange rates and resources outside the reporting system affect the result.
humanitarian_resource_gaps.boundary: Require valid plan and funding records without duplicates. Missing funding reports are not a verified zero gap, and promises of funding are not money received. Keep the last validated result and show its age.

carbon_monoxide.method: Keep emissions separate from concentrations measured indoors or outdoors. Retain the monitoring method used.
carbon_monoxide.uncertainty: A concentration combines several possible sources with air movement and ventilation.
carbon_monoxide.boundary: Do not assign a reading to one source without an assessment that defines and supports that connection.

gulf_stream_slowdown.method: Identify the exact section of current, depths, period and measuring instruments. Keep calibration and tidal corrections, gaps and uncertainty. Distinguish current position from water volume carried, and the Florida Current from the wider Gulf Stream and Atlantic overturning circulation.
gulf_stream_slowdown.uncertainty: The current carries more water farther downstream, and different depths can change differently. Wind-driven circulation and overturning are not the same, while instrument corrections affect trends.
gulf_stream_slowdown.boundary: One section does not represent the whole current or Atlantic circulation. Do not infer collapse from short-term variation or use coastal sea level alone as proof of changing currents.

solar_radiation_trapping.method: Use checked global concentrations of each long-lived greenhouse gas to calculate the extra energy retained, following the named assessment equations. Keep the preindustrial comparison, gases included, overlapping absorption and uncertainty clear.
solar_radiation_trapping.uncertainty: Some gases have few measurements. Calibration, gas lifetimes, overlapping heat absorption and the atmosphere's rapid adjustments affect the estimated contribution of each gas and the total.
solar_radiation_trapping.boundary: Gas emitted, concentration at one place, heat flow and surface temperature are different from this measure of extra energy retained. They must not be substituted for it.

ocean_heat_content.method: Calculate heat change from the temperature departure, seawater density and the energy needed to warm it, over the stated area and depth. Keep the reference period, mapping method and observing instruments clear.
ocean_heat_content.uncertainty: Deep-ocean readings are sparse. Instrument biases, float coverage, mapping, salt content and reference choices affect the estimate.
ocean_heat_content.boundary: A regional heat change cannot be applied to the entire ocean. Missing readings do not mean no change in heat.

peatland_degradations.method: Keep peatland boundaries, condition categories, drainage, land use and fire history with the map. Compare the same classifications through time.
peatland_degradations.uncertainty: Peat depth, drainage maps, clouds, land-cover labels, restoration and differences between national records affect estimates.
peatland_degradations.boundary: Fire, emissions or land-cover change alone do not establish peatland damage when the peatland's extent and condition have not been checked.

waterborne_pathogen_outbreaks.method: Keep suspected, probable and confirmed illness cases separate. Identify the germ, exposure route, laboratory results and investigation status.
waterborne_pathogen_outbreaks.uncertainty: Missed cases, time between exposure and illness, and several possible exposure routes make causes difficult to separate.
waterborne_pathogen_outbreaks.boundary: Describe risk rather than a confirmed outbreak until the local health investigation supports that conclusion.

emergency_response_overload.method: Keep monthly incident counts, response priorities, service area, target times and the share meeting them. Subtract that percentage from 100 to estimate the share missing the goal. Any derived missed-incident count is approximate because the source percentages are rounded.
emergency_response_overload.uncertainty: Distance, traffic, call types, dispatch choices and staff availability can all affect response time. Aggregated records, changing goals, mutual aid and incomplete months also affect comparisons.
emergency_response_overload.boundary: Require valid targets, counts and percentages for at least 24 months without duplicates. Missing a response goal does not prove patient harm or an overloaded service. This local measure cannot represent national emergency performance.

zoonotic_disease_outbreaks.method: Identify the germ, case definition, illness and reporting dates, laboratory method and location. Keep evidence about animal hosts and exposure routes, the population counted and reporting delays clear.
zoonotic_disease_outbreaks.uncertainty: Missed cases, changing definitions, access to testing and gaps in animal monitoring affect estimates. The animal source may remain uncertain.
zoonotic_disease_outbreaks.boundary: Do not combine unrelated diseases into one causal trend or assume an animal source without investigation. Possible exposure is not confirmed transmission.

alpine_snowpack_declines.method: Keep elevation, whether precipitation fell as rain or snow, temperature and the method used to estimate water stored in snow. Retain surface reflectivity and a matching seasonal reference.
alpine_snowpack_declines.uncertainty: Few mountain gauges, complex terrain, clouds and changes between rain and snow make estimates uncertain.
alpine_snowpack_declines.boundary: One warm day or a regional yearly temperature does not establish declining mountain snowpack.

wetlands_drainage_scales.method: Use the source's total area of drained organic soils. Keep cropland and grassland parts separate when examining them. A yearly area total describes land already drained, not new drainage during that year.
wetlands_drainage_scales.uncertainty: Peat-soil maps, yearly land cover, farming classifications, boundaries and standard estimation methods affect the area. Source warnings and revisions must be retained.
wetlands_drainage_scales.boundary: This farming-related measure does not cover every wetland, forestry drainage, peat extraction or newly converted area. Missing records are not zero.

subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.method: Assess whether cable systems share landing areas, power, stations or land routes, using appropriately generalised locations. Keep ownership, active and possible capacity, alternative routes, repair access and outage duration separate.
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.uncertainty: Public maps simplify routes and some details are confidential. Different owners or cable counts do not guarantee independent operation, and traffic can move to other routes.
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.boundary: Do not expose sensitive facility details. Several nearby cables are not automatically independent backups, and physical exposure does not prove service loss without evidence about the network and its recovery options.

rice_paddy_methane_bubbles.method: Use field measurements or a stated inventory method. Keep the rice area, growing season, water management, added organic material and soil type clear.
rice_paddy_methane_bubbles.uncertainty: Methane release changes with water levels, soil, temperature, organic material and crop management.
rice_paddy_methane_bubbles.boundary: Visible bubbles or the area planted with rice are not measurements of methane emissions.

jet_stream_volatility.method: Calculate the chosen jet-stream measure from a named weather dataset and atmospheric height. Compare matching seasons against a fixed reference and test how the result changes with the definition used.
jet_stream_volatility.uncertainty: The index, dataset and season matter. Tropical conditions, upper-atmosphere influences and natural variability can all change the pattern.
jet_stream_volatility.boundary: Do not claim a human-caused trend when the record, definition or uncertainty estimate is insufficient.

glacier_calving_events.method: Keep the glacier's shape, front position, speed, thickness and grounded boundary with the event record. Identify the sensor and separate ordinary iceberg release from sustained retreat or break-up.
glacier_calving_events.uncertainty: Clouds, floating ice debris, unclear front boundaries and poorly measured underwater geometry affect estimates of event size and ice loss.
glacier_calving_events.boundary: One iceberg breaking off does not prove climate-driven retreat. A longer record of the glacier front and overall ice gain or loss is needed.

wildfire_smoke_hospitalization_burden.method: Keep the diagnosis group, population, time delay after exposure, method and evidence linking admissions to smoke.
wildfire_smoke_hospitalization_burden.uncertainty: Hospital admissions have several possible causes, and the part due to smoke is uncertain.
wildfire_smoke_hospitalization_burden.boundary: Do not describe all admissions for breathing problems as caused by wildfire.

cooling_equity_gaps.method: Combine heat exposure with housing, electricity reliability, cooling access, costs and vulnerability. Owning a cooling device does not prove that it works well or can be afforded when needed.
cooling_equity_gaps.uncertainty: Homes and power supplies differ. So do indoor heat, cooling equipment, prices and what people can afford. People also move between places. These differences make groups harder to compare.
cooling_equity_gaps.boundary: National electricity access or air-conditioner sales do not establish fair access to safe cooling. Show gaps in household and service-quality data.

kelp_forest_collapse.method: Keep kelp species, sensor or survey method, tide, season, mapped area and reference period clear. Check clouds and water conditions that can hide the plants.
kelp_forest_collapse.uncertainty: Storms, seasons, water clarity and the natural life cycle can change visible kelp cover without the same amount of lasting ecological loss.
kelp_forest_collapse.boundary: One obscured image does not prove loss. Compare matching seasons, sensors and coastline boundaries.

trophic_cascade_collapses.method: Measure predators, prey and the resources below them, with evidence of feeding relationships. Keep study design, time delays, alternative explanations and uncertainty clear.
trophic_cascade_collapses.uncertainty: Other consumers may compensate for a loss, diets can change and feeding relationships differ by setting.
trophic_cascade_collapses.boundary: One declining species does not prove a chain reaction through a food web. Intermediate and later responses must also be measured.

aquifer_recharge_failure.method: Account for rain, snowmelt, plant water use, land cover and the properties of soil and underground rock. Keep river leakage, pumping, modelling method and the period used to check the model.
aquifer_recharge_failure.uncertainty: Groundwater replenishment is often estimated with models rather than measured directly. Geology, earlier soil wetness, land cover and climate strongly affect it.
aquifer_recharge_failure.boundary: Falling groundwater alone does not prove less replenishment. Increased pumping or water leaving the underground store can also lower levels.

cloud_albedo_shift.method: Compare cloudy and clear conditions using one consistent radiation convention. Keep measurements at Earth's surface separate from those at the top of the atmosphere. Report reflected sunlight, trapped outgoing heat and their combined balance separately.
cloud_albedo_shift.uncertainty: Cloud identification, time of day, instrument calibration, particles above clouds and surface reflectivity can change the estimate.
cloud_albedo_shift.boundary: A reflectivity change without its direction cannot be labelled warming or cooling. One cloud property alone does not establish a climate feedback without energy-flow observations.

deep_sea_mining_dust.method: Keep the mined material, sediment amount, discharge rate and depth, particle size, water turbulence and background particles clear. Retain sensor limits, model assumptions and uncertainty.
deep_sea_mining_dust.uncertainty: Full-scale plume behaviour depends on discharge design, turbulence and particles joining together or settling. Natural cloudy layers can complicate detection.
deep_sea_mining_dust.boundary: A modelled plume area alone does not establish ecological harm. Natural suspended sediment must not be labelled mining waste.

agrochemical_water_sinks.method: Identify each farm chemical and breakdown product, laboratory method and detection limit. Keep dissolved and total amounts separate, with water flow, rain, land use, sampling times and the version of any safety comparison used.
agrochemical_water_sinks.uncertainty: Short pollution pulses can be missed. Mixtures, breakdown products, flow, season, treatment, urban sources and changing laboratory methods affect what is detected.
agrochemical_water_sinks.boundary: Do not add different chemicals without explaining the weighting. A non-detection is not necessarily zero, nearby farming does not prove the source, and detecting a residue alone does not prove harm.

acid_rain_deposition.method: Keep chemicals deposited in rain or snow separate from dry particles and gases. Record the substance, precipitation amount, sampling time, wind context and method.
acid_rain_deposition.uncertainty: Chemical reactions, weather and the distance pollutants travel affect how much reaches a site.
acid_rain_deposition.boundary: Emissions at a source are not the same as pollution deposited at a particular destination.

desertification_frontiers.method: Use a fixed definition and boundary for the dryland area. Compare land cover, plant productivity, soil and vegetation over time, keeping climate, management, restoration and the criteria for damage clear.
desertification_frontiers.uncertainty: Weather variation, sensor changes, grazing, crop cycles, soil sampling and reference choices can alter the apparent area and direction of change.
desertification_frontiers.boundary: Dry climate, drought, bare ground or one poor vegetation year does not prove lasting degradation. Several indicators and a consistent area are needed.

cfc_saturated_layers.method: Keep each gas separate, including its chlorine or bromine content, ozone-damaging strength, concentration and lifetime. Account for the time taken to reach the upper atmosphere and keep location, calibration, natural sources and uncertainty clear.
cfc_saturated_layers.uncertainty: Gases differ in lifetime, transport and how effectively they damage ozone. A surface concentration is not the same as the amount of reactive chemicals high in the atmosphere.
cfc_saturated_layers.boundary: Do not add gases without appropriate weights or label HFC replacements as ozone-damaging. One surface sample does not show current upper-atmosphere loading, and a falling total does not mean every gas is declining.

rainforest_savannization.method: Define what counts as forest and a changed vegetation type before comparing maps. Keep sensor, fire and logging history, reference period, rainfall context and the minimum time the new state must persist.
rainforest_savannization.uncertainty: Seasonal changes, temporary canopy loss, fire scars, plantations and sensor changes can look like a lasting shift to a different ecosystem.
rainforest_savannization.boundary: Do not claim a lasting forest-to-open-land transition when only temporary damage or canopy loss has been observed.

urban_water_rationing_zones.method: Keep the legal reason for restrictions, available supply, exemptions and the period when rules apply.
urban_water_rationing_zones.uncertainty: Restriction rules differ between water utilities and jurisdictions.
urban_water_rationing_zones.boundary: Limited water does not prove rationing unless the utility has actually introduced restrictions.

genetic_diversity_bottlenecks.method: Keep the population counted separate from the number effectively contributing genes to later generations. Record genetic methods, sampling, generation time, movement between groups, family relationships, historical reference and confidence limits.
genetic_diversity_bottlenecks.uncertainty: Genetic markers, timing, population structure, immigration and small samples affect inferred variety and breeding population size.
genetic_diversity_bottlenecks.boundary: Few individuals or fragmented habitat alone do not prove a genetic bottleneck. Genetic or family-history evidence is needed.

palm_oil_canopy_clearance.method: Compare reviewed oil-palm maps with observed tree-cover loss. Check that forest existed before plantation expansion and verify when conversion happened. Tree-cover loss is not always deforestation or caused by oil palm.
palm_oil_canopy_clearance.uncertainty: Plantation boundaries may be incomplete. Replanting, fire, earlier damage, canopy definitions and timing differences affect how causes are assigned.
palm_oil_canopy_clearance.boundary: When earlier forest cover or conversion timing cannot be verified, report the observed tree-cover change without claiming oil palm caused it. Keep that causal question under review.

fishery_border_dispute_zones.method: Keep original incident reports, participants, countries, fishery, location and jurisdiction. Distinguish enforcement, detention, coercion and violence. Retain catch, fishing effort, stock condition, dependence and agreements, and remove duplicate news reports.
fishery_border_dispute_zones.uncertainty: Public reporting is uneven and politically influenced. Incidents can mix fishing, territory, security and other motives, while fish-stock and social data may cover different places or periods.
fishery_border_dispute_zones.boundary: Coinciding scarcity or warming does not prove a conflict's cause. Nearby vessels are not evidence of hostility. Illegal fishing, enforcement, territorial disputes and armed conflict must not be treated as one category.

inland_waterway_fuel_spills.method: Keep the incident identifier, location, spilled material, volume, release route, response status and uncertainty.
inland_waterway_fuel_spills.uncertainty: Investigations may revise the amount spilled and where it travelled downstream.
inland_waterway_fuel_spills.boundary: Vessel traffic or fuel stored near water does not prove an oil discharge.

coral_reef_fragmentation.method: Record the cause of breakage, reef zone, coral type, earlier structure and survey detail. Keep fragment size, living tissue and recovery status clear.
coral_reef_fragmentation.uncertainty: Missing pre-event surveys, poor visibility, overlapping stresses and buried fragments can affect damage estimates.
coral_reef_fragmentation.boundary: Bleaching, death or low coral cover does not by itself prove physical fragmentation. Actual breakage, displacement or gaps in the reef structure must be observed.

dust_storm_frequency.method: Use a fixed definition for a dust event and keep wind, soil moisture, land cover and suspected sources clear. Retain ground readings, satellite product, plume boundary, duration, detection limits and missing observations.
dust_storm_frequency.uncertainty: Clouds, sparse monitors, event thresholds, smoke mixed with dust and changing satellite methods can affect counts and exposure estimates.
dust_storm_frequency.boundary: Do not combine incompatible event definitions or assume a distant dust plume was caused by land management. Missing observations do not mean no event.

pollen_allergen_spikes.method: Keep plant species, sampler, counting method, station and rules for the start and end of the season. Record total counts alongside weather, vegetation, missing days and quality checks.
pollen_allergen_spikes.uncertainty: Different samplers may give different absolute counts. Wind transport, rain, local plants and season definitions also affect results.
pollen_allergen_spikes.boundary: Compare matching sampling methods. Airborne pollen does not identify its local plant source, and a longer season is not the same as more intense exposure.

estuary_eutrophication.method: Keep nutrient type, concentration and total amount delivered separate. Record water flow, algae, clarity, oxygen depth, salt content and how long water stays in the estuary. Distinguish observed from modelled results.
estuary_eutrophication.uncertainty: Tides, river flow, stored nutrients, water layers, algae types, sensor drift and sparse sampling affect the estimated extent and cause.
estuary_eutrophication.boundary: One nutrient sample does not establish a problem throughout an estuary. Algae, low oxygen or runoff need evidence from the receiving water before the wider condition is claimed.

avian_migration_disruptions.method: Keep bird species or radar target, survey effort and detection method clear. Compare route, arrival and departure dates with food timing, habitat and weather, using a fixed reference and accounting for missing observations.
avian_migration_disruptions.uncertainty: Radar may not identify species, and volunteer survey effort changes. Birds use different routes and timing cues, so an earlier arrival does not automatically mean harm.
avian_migration_disruptions.boundary: Do not combine birds with different migration strategies into one trend. A mapped flyway is not an observed journey, and a timing change alone does not prove population damage or a climate cause.

shell_calcification_failures.method: Pair checked seawater chemistry with the species, life stage, temperature and food supply. Measure shell growth or survival directly rather than assuming failure from acidity alone.
shell_calcification_failures.uncertainty: Responses differ greatly between species, ages, previous exposure and other stresses.
shell_calcification_failures.boundary: Show insufficient evidence if either the chemistry or biological response is missing or cannot be compared.

amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.method: Distinguish the two fungal diseases, Bd and Bsal, and keep host species, life stage, swab and laboratory methods clear. Separate infection from diagnosed disease and death, retaining survey effort, weather, prior exposure and population trends.
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.uncertainty: Detection varies with sampling, season, temperature and infection level. Infection may be widespread without visible disease or deaths caused by it.
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.boundary: A positive swab does not prove decline or death. Do not combine the fungi, compare incompatible tests or assign unexplained deaths to one germ. Temperature associations are not universal causal rules.

black_carbon_deposition.method: Match soot deposited on snow or ice with nearby measurements of reflectivity, snow-grain size and melt conditions. Emissions alone do not show how much reached the surface.
black_carbon_deposition.uncertainty: Deposits vary greatly over short distances. Dust, snow age, meltwater and sensor methods also affect darkening.
black_carbon_deposition.boundary: One sample cannot represent all snow and ice. State when coverage is insufficient.

glacial_siltation_streams.method: Pair sediment concentration, or a checked water-cloudiness measure, with river flow. Keep glacier cover, season, event type, particle sizes and the material excluded from sampling clear.
glacial_siltation_streams.uncertainty: Brief peaks, sparse winter observations, changing drainage and station placement affect yearly totals. Cloudiness-to-sediment relationships can change as flows rise and fall.
glacial_siltation_streams.boundary: Meltwater volume, cloudiness or glacier retreat alone does not measure sediment carried. A conversion checked in one basin must not be used elsewhere without validation.

jellyfish_swarm_surges.method: Keep jellyfish species and life stage, survey effort and local conditions clear. Include attachment surfaces, temperature, salt, oxygen, nutrients, food, predators, fishing and currents.
jellyfish_swarm_surges.uncertainty: Jellyfish occur in patches and have changing life stages. Currents, uneven observations and occasional large releases of young animals make trends difficult to establish.
jellyfish_swarm_surges.boundary: Beach strandings, clogged intakes or one survey do not prove a regional increase. Comparable abundance measurements and a fixed reference are needed.

bark_beetle_epidemics.method: Identify beetle and tree species, tree density, survey method and the evidence assigning deaths to beetles. Keep the relevant drought, temperature and fire periods with the mapped area.
bark_beetle_epidemics.uncertainty: Aerial surveys can miss lighter damage, and identifying causes gets harder after needles fall. Several causes of death may overlap.
bark_beetle_epidemics.boundary: Do not assign all drought or fire-related tree death to beetles. Different species respond differently to climate, and canopy colour alone does not measure outbreak intensity.

old_growth_forest_logging.method: State what counts as old-growth forest in this setting. Keep harvesting type and intensity, roads, earlier carbon and habitat structure, use of harvested wood and regrowth plans clear.
old_growth_forest_logging.uncertainty: Definitions differ between forests and jurisdictions. Remote images can miss selective cutting and damage to surrounding trees.
old_growth_forest_logging.boundary: Not all management of mature trees is old-growth logging. Net emissions require accounting for both the forest and what happens to harvested wood.

savannah_tree_cover_decline.method: Keep the savanna definition, tree and grass cover, measuring method and rainfall clear. Record drought, fire timing and severity, grazing, clearing and recovery.
savannah_tree_cover_decline.uncertainty: Rain, fire control, grazing, browsing and woody plant expansion can produce opposite trends. Sensor definitions also matter.
savannah_tree_cover_decline.boundary: Low tree cover is not always damage. One fire, dry season or image does not establish a lasting decline.

pesticide_spray_drift_zones.method: Identify the chemical, mixture, spraying equipment, droplet size, amount and intended treatment area. Keep wind, temperature, still-air layers, distance to exposed places, sample type, detection limits and product rules clear.
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.uncertainty: Wind and heat change where spray goes and how fast its water dries. The equipment, when samples are taken and how fast chemicals break down also matter. Missing records of spraying make exposure harder to estimate.
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.boundary: Proximity or a complaint alone does not prove exposure. Do not combine different chemicals or assume that a permitted application drifted beyond its target.

snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.method: Record particle type and size, dust amount, position within the snow and how it arrived. Keep snow depth, stored water, reflectivity, grain size, sunlight, clouds, sensor, melt stage and reference period clear.
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.uncertainty: Dust can be buried and reappear during melting. Soot, algae, forest debris, snow-grain growth, slope and sensor detail also affect how dark the snow looks.
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.boundary: Dark snow alone does not measure dust mass, and mineral dust is different from soot. Compare matching melt stages and methods. Results from Colorado need local checks before use in another region.

heavy_metal_bioaccumulation.method: Identify the metal and its chemical form, sample material, species and tissue. Keep animal size, age, diet level, wet or dry weight, likely source and detection limit clear.
heavy_metal_bioaccumulation.uncertainty: Metals differ in how easily bodies absorb, use and remove them. Diet, growth, season and food-web structure also change accumulation.
heavy_metal_bioaccumulation.boundary: Do not combine metals or equate detection with poisoning. Increasing concentration up a food chain needs evidence at several feeding levels.

wetland_peat_fires.method: Match checked fire detections or boundaries with confirmed peatland maps. Keep burn depth, duration, moisture and the assumptions used to estimate emissions, including limits from clouds and smoke.
wetland_peat_fires.uncertainty: Underground smouldering is hard to observe. Burn depth, peat density, repeat fires and uncertain emission rates can produce large differences in estimates.
wetland_peat_fires.boundary: A wetland fire is not necessarily burning peat. Confirm the peatland location, and do not turn missing burned-area records into zero.

convective_instability_shift.method: Keep the full vertical temperature and moisture profile and the method used to estimate rising-air energy. Also record layers that block rising air, winds changing with height and the trigger that could lift the air.
convective_instability_shift.uncertainty: Results change with the air parcel chosen and the accuracy of moisture readings. Models and satellites can smooth important layers, while simple calculations may overstate the energy a real updraft uses.
convective_instability_shift.boundary: CAPE, a measure of potential rising-air energy, alone cannot predict a storm, hail, tornadoes, lightning or heavy rain. Other conditions and observed outcomes are needed.

riparian_zone_erosion.method: Keep river-bank material, shape, plants, roots and water speed with repeated surveys. Record rain, channel changes, land use and any protective works.
riparian_zone_erosion.uncertainty: Bank retreat often happens in bursts. Ground type, vegetation, floods, dams, grazing and the time between surveys affect measured rates.
riparian_zone_erosion.boundary: Sparse plants or high river flow alone do not prove erosion. Repeated bank measurements, observed collapse or sediment evidence are needed.

nighttime_heat_retention.method: Pair comparable air-temperature readings from the built-up area and its reference area. Keep sensor height, location, local time, weather and season clear. Surface temperatures remain a different measure.
nighttime_heat_retention.uncertainty: Buildings, wind, clouds, moisture and the choice of rural comparison affect the temperature difference.
nighttime_heat_retention.boundary: Do not mix satellite surface temperatures with near-ground air readings. One unpaired station cannot establish a citywide difference.

biodiversity_corridors_disruption.method: Keep measures of forest-patch connections separate from connections among protected areas. Use forest-loss history only to help understand whether the pattern has persisted.
biodiversity_corridors_disruption.uncertainty: Connected shapes on a map do not prove animals can move between them. Map detail, patch-size rules and protected-area boundaries affect estimates.
biodiversity_corridors_disruption.boundary: Maps alone do not establish wildlife use, breeding exchange, population benefit or one universal measure of corridor quality.

walker_circulation_shift.method: Keep the circulation-index definition, pressure and wind areas, atmospheric height, weather dataset and reference period clear. Retain Pacific warm or cool phase, rainfall, season, smoothing and missing data.
walker_circulation_shift.uncertainty: Different indices, sparse early observations, model changes, volcanic influences and natural decade-scale variation can alter the apparent trend or even its direction.
walker_circulation_shift.boundary: One Pacific event or a short record does not establish a long-term human-caused trend. Convert indices with opposite signs consistently, and do not treat one pressure reading as the whole circulation.

fjord_sedimentation_pulses.method: Identify the coastal inlet and glacier, distance from the ice front, sampling method and season.
fjord_sedimentation_pulses.uncertainty: Sediment delivery depends on stored material, iceberg release, drainage routes and the shape of the inlet.
fjord_sedimentation_pulses.boundary: Glacier retreat rate alone does not measure sediment delivery.

transformer_heat_failure_risk.method: Keep the transformer's rated capacity, actual load, air and internal temperatures, cooling, age and insulation condition. Retain alarms and outages. Estimate ageing only with a documented model suited to the equipment.
transformer_heat_failure_risk.uncertainty: Sensors may miss the hottest internal point. Cooling, moisture, earlier damage, electrical conditions and equipment design affect the estimated risk.
transformer_heat_failure_risk.boundary: Regional heat or system demand alone does not prove a transformer failed. Equipment-level temperature, load, condition or a documented outage is needed.

freeze_thaw_rock_fracturing.method: Keep the slope, rock crack, temperature period, water source and monitoring method with the movement record.
freeze_thaw_rock_fracturing.uncertainty: Rockfalls have several triggers, and local rock properties strongly affect whether blocks become unstable.
freeze_thaw_rock_fracturing.boundary: Air temperature or freezing alone does not prove a rockfall occurred.

overstory_tree_mortality.method: Keep tree species, size, health and the definition of upper-canopy trees clear. Record heat and drought, insects, disease, fire injury, competition, management and time between exposure and death.
overstory_tree_mortality.uncertainty: Several pressures often act together, and a tree can die long after damage. This makes the main cause difficult to separate.
overstory_tree_mortality.boundary: Discoloured foliage or a total loss of trees does not establish a cause without field observations and evidence about timing and disturbance.

aerosolized_microplastics.method: Record the air volume or collection area sampled, particle-size limits, sampler, contamination checks and laboratory confirmation of plastic type. Keep particle shape and any validated mass separate, alongside weather and likely travel routes.
aerosolized_microplastics.uncertainty: Contamination and mistaken visual identification can strongly affect results. Sampling methods, size limits and incomplete chemical checks make studies difficult to compare.
aerosolized_microplastics.boundary: A visible fibre is not confirmed plastic. Do not compare incompatible methods, turn counts into mass without particle evidence, infer health harm from detection alone or call one sample a global trend.

coastal_saltwater_intrusion.method: Keep well depth, underground water layer, height reference, pumping period and the method used to measure salt. Retain local sea-level conditions.
coastal_saltwater_intrusion.uncertainty: Salt can arrive through different routes, and local rock and water conditions strongly affect its movement.
coastal_saltwater_intrusion.boundary: Sea level, pumping or salt in an unrelated well alone does not prove saltwater has entered this freshwater source.

coastal_groundwater_withdrawal.method: Keep well depth, underground water layer, height reference, pumping period and the method used to measure salt. Retain local sea-level conditions.
coastal_groundwater_withdrawal.uncertainty: Salt can arrive through different routes, and local rock and water conditions strongly affect its movement.
coastal_groundwater_withdrawal.boundary: Sea level, pumping or salt in an unrelated well alone does not prove saltwater has entered this freshwater source.

tundra_shrubification_speeds.method: Identify the shrub species, field plot or map cell, season, method and local water conditions.
tundra_shrubification_speeds.uncertainty: Greening and shrub growth vary by species, region and disturbance history.
tundra_shrubification_speeds.boundary: Regional warming or a satellite greenness reading alone does not establish shrub expansion.

subpolar_gyre_weakening.method: Define the northern Atlantic circulation area, depth and period. Keep sea height, winds, temperature, salt, density and current readings with their methods. Distinguish flow strength, area, position and water properties.
subpolar_gyre_weakening.uncertainty: There is no single universal index. Sea height reflects both water mass and expansion, while winds and density changes can act in opposite directions. Horizontal circulation is different from Atlantic overturning.
subpolar_gyre_weakening.boundary: Regional cooling or one sea-height reading does not prove weaker circulation. Do not combine incompatible indices or treat one decade-long phase as a steady climate trend.

shelf_sea_hypoxia.method: Keep oxygen readings with depth, height above the seabed, instrument checks, temperature and salt content. State the low-oxygen threshold, area surveyed and whether the result is observed or modelled.
shelf_sea_hypoxia.uncertainty: Sparse survey lines, sensor drift, brief mixing events, tides and the way gaps are filled affect estimated area and duration.
shelf_sea_hypoxia.boundary: One low-oxygen station does not represent an entire shallow sea. Global trends cannot replace local readings, and different depth or threshold definitions must remain separate.

freshwater_mussel_depletion.method: Identify mussel species, life stage and fish hosts, keeping survey effort and detection limits clear. Record flow, temperature, riverbed conditions, barriers, pollutants, disease and drought.
freshwater_mussel_depletion.uncertainty: Mussel beds are patchy and individuals live a long time. Irregular reproduction, changing fish hosts and several possible causes of death make trends uncertain.
freshwater_mussel_depletion.boundary: Absence or one survey does not establish a cause. A local decline must not be generalised to other species or river basins.

lightning_regime_shifts.method: Keep the lightning sensor, version, detection efficiency and rules for grouping signals into flashes. Separate all lightning from strikes reaching the ground, retaining area, season, viewing time and missing coverage.
lightning_regime_shifts.uncertainty: Satellites and ground networks detect different parts of lightning. Upgrades, viewing geometry, day or night conditions and short records can create apparent changes.
lightning_regime_shifts.boundary: A satellite light event is not necessarily a ground strike. Do not infer climate trends from coverage changes or turn flash counts directly into fire or severe-storm probabilities.

coral_larval_mortality.method: Identify coral species, life stage, parent condition, temperature and seawater chemistry. Keep settlement surface, observation length, method and the number of young animals followed.
coral_larval_mortality.uncertainty: Spawning, transport, predators, settlement conditions, parent health, disease and sampling time all affect survival.
coral_larval_mortality.boundary: Adult bleaching, low reef cover or missing new colonies alone do not prove larval deaths. Observations of the relevant life stage are needed.

riverine_habitat_fragmentation.method: Keep connections along a whole river separate from connections between its source and the ocean. Preserve the source's distinction between long rivers and the full mapped network.
riverine_habitat_fragmentation.uncertainty: Usable connections depend on species, age, flow and scale. A statistic about long rivers does not describe every stream.
riverine_habitat_fragmentation.boundary: Global statistics cannot show whether one species passes a barrier or whether a particular small stream has good habitat.

high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.method: Define forest and treeline consistently, recording species, height, slope, map method and field checks. Keep snow, moisture, drought, fire, insects, regrowth and land use alongside a rule for how long a change must last.
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.uncertainty: Upper forest edges can expand while dry lower edges retreat. Fire, harvesting, delayed regrowth and mapping changes can look like a permanent climate-driven shift.
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.boundary: One fire scar is not range contraction. Treeline movement alone does not establish overall forest loss, and warming can have opposite effects at cold and dry boundaries.

atmospheric_river_intensification.method: Keep the method used to identify the moist-air band, its water-transport threshold, shape, landfall, direction, duration and peak strength. Retain rainfall, earlier soil and snow conditions, river gauges and missing periods.
atmospheric_river_intensification.uncertainty: Catalogues use different thresholds, models and definitions of landfall. Mountains and earlier ground conditions strongly affect rain and runoff impacts.
atmospheric_river_intensification.boundary: Compare matching detection methods. Not every moisture plume reaches land, and water-vapour transport alone does not establish flood damage.

blue_carbon_habitat_loss.method: Keep coastal habitat type, mapped area, soil depth, carbon measurement, disturbance and reference year clear. Separate carbon actually released from carbon that would otherwise have been absorbed later.
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.uncertainty: Carbon below ground, the fate of eroded material, decay rates and mapping detail differ between habitats and methods.
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.boundary: Habitat area cannot be converted directly to emissions without evidence about its carbon stores and the type of damage.

methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.method: State how the air's methane-removal capacity is defined and averaged. Keep methane, other reactive gases, moisture, ozone, fires and lightning in the chemical model, along with the observations used to check it.
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.uncertainty: Hydroxyl radicals last too briefly for a dense global monitoring network. Models disagree about trends and are sensitive to emissions, chemistry, air movement and how places are weighted.
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.boundary: Methane growth alone does not show a global decline in removal capacity. Compare matching lifetime definitions, and do not assign changes to one gas without checking the wider chemistry.

stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.method: Keep total ozone through the atmosphere separate from the size of the Antarctic ozone hole and its minimum ozone value. Use the stated 220-Dobson-unit threshold and fixed seasonal windows, retaining satellite methods, gaps and quality context.
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.uncertainty: Polar winds, temperature, sunlight, particles, transport and sensor changes affect each year's result. The chosen seasonal window also matters.
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.boundary: Upper-atmosphere ozone is different from ground-level pollution. Antarctica does not represent the whole globe. Leave the missing 1995 year missing, and do not explain one unusual season without chemical and weather evidence.

aviation_condensation_trails.method: Keep flight-identification limits, altitude, temperature, humidity and whether the air supports ice growth. Distinguish trails from natural thin clouds and record persistence, spreading, day or night and the method used to estimate their energy effect.
aviation_condensation_trails.uncertainty: Natural clouds, overlapping layers, humidity forecasts and satellite detection make attribution difficult. Cloud properties and the balance between daytime reflection and heat trapping also matter.
aviation_condensation_trails.boundary: Do not infer deliberate dispersal or assign a trail to one aircraft without matching flight-path evidence. A trail's presence alone cannot be converted into warming.

fisheries_range_redistribution.method: Identify the fish species and stock, survey equipment, effort, season, depth and area. Keep how average position and range edges are calculated, along with temperature, oxygen, fishing boundaries and missing years.
fisheries_range_redistribution.uncertainty: Survey coverage, how easily fish are caught, seasonal movement, age, population size, food and fishing pressure can all look like a range shift.
fisheries_range_redistribution.boundary: Landings alone do not prove a climate cause. Do not mix stocks or seasons, or extend results outside the survey area without an explicit model.

food_insecurity.method: Use the provider's food-access estimates with their uncertainty. Keep difficulty obtaining food separate from measured biological outcomes such as undernutrition.
food_insecurity.uncertainty: Survey and model uncertainty differs by country and release. Providers may revise earlier years.
food_insecurity.boundary: Keep the last reviewed release and show its age. A missing country-year is not zero hardship.

nutrient_pollution.method: Make chemical type, measured fraction, units, method and quality checks comparable before combining water records. Keep global nitrogen losses, financial costs and affected-water inventories separate, with their own time periods.
nutrient_pollution.uncertainty: Sampling frequency, detection limits and changing methods affect local trends. Global budgets combine several routes, and affected-site inventories may miss unmonitored places.
nutrient_pollution.boundary: Withhold local summaries with inadequate coverage. Do not apply a US reading globally, convert site counts to area or assign a global cost to one river basin.

seagrass_meadow_decline.method: Use reviewed habitat boundaries to measure seagrass area change. Species sighting records can help check the maps but cannot show that seagrass is absent elsewhere.
seagrass_meadow_decline.uncertainty: Map age, classification, season and incomplete repeat surveys limit comparisons.
seagrass_meadow_decline.boundary: Do not update habitat area from raw sightings. Keep the previous mapped boundaries with their uncertainty until a comparable map is available.

urban_heat_island.method: Keep surface heating separate from the temperature of air around buildings. State the urban boundary, rural comparison, day or night, season and sensor or model version.
urban_heat_island.uncertainty: Boundary choices, height, building layout, weather, changing land cover and measurement methods affect comparisons.
urban_heat_island.boundary: Keep the previous value if changed boundaries or processing cannot be applied consistently to earlier data.

dam_and_diversion_infrastructure.method: Keep the share of long rivers that do not flow freely and the leading barrier types identified by the source. Natural barriers remain separate from human-built structures.
dam_and_diversion_infrastructure.uncertainty: Connectivity varies between tributaries, flows and species. Global inventories can miss small structures or recent changes.
dam_and_diversion_infrastructure.boundary: The global share does not count structures or show whether a particular species can pass one. It also does not measure local service loss.

road_stream_crossing_barriers.method: Classify stream crossings using surveyed dimensions, water flows and evidence of animal passage. Keep an unknown category for crossings without enough information.
road_stream_crossing_barriers.uncertainty: Passage changes with river flow, species, the structure's condition and survey method.
road_stream_crossing_barriers.boundary: Unsurveyed crossings are unknown, not automatically barriers.

levee_and_channelization_works.method: Map where engineering confines or straightens a river. Compare flooding and side-to-side habitat connections with a specified reference stretch.
levee_and_channelization_works.uncertainty: Historical reference choices, flood height and map detail affect connectivity estimates.
levee_and_channelization_works.boundary: An embankment's presence alone does not establish that a floodplain is disconnected. The river stretch must be mapped.

humanitarian_response_funding_shortfall.method: For each aid plan and year, subtract reported paid or committed funding from the current revised requirement. Shortfall cannot fall below zero, but coverage may exceed 100%. Keep pledges separate and exclude them from received or committed funding.
humanitarian_response_funding_shortfall.uncertainty: The reporting system does not capture every resource or show aid delivered. Delays, unlinked funds, exchange rates and revised requirements affect the result.
humanitarian_response_funding_shortfall.boundary: Reject missing, duplicate or invalid records. Use revised requirements when available, keep the last validated result if updates fail, and never treat pledges as funding or funding as proof of delivery.

humanitarian_access_constraints.method: Keep the source's count and share of countries with ACAPS access scores from 3 to 5. Retain improved, worsened and stable categories separately. Derive the total countries assessed only by adding those non-overlapping categories, clearly labelling the total as calculated.
humanitarian_access_constraints.uncertainty: Analysts combine available reports, which may miss local variation. Conflict, information access, crisis definitions and revisions affect comparisons.
humanitarian_access_constraints.boundary: Require complete, consistent counts, percentages and methods. Country-level summaries do not measure people reached, aid delivered or conditions in one specific country, and missing reports do not prove unrestricted access.

humanitarian_surge_demand.method: Compare each plan's current revised financial requirement with its original requirement. Count only positive increases in this measure and calculate their share of the positive original amount. Keep decreases and unchanged plans separately.
humanitarian_surge_demand.uncertainty: A budget increase can reflect prices, scope, priorities or corrections as well as greater needs. It is not a direct count of newly affected people.
humanitarian_surge_demand.boundary: Require complete, positive original requirements and valid revised amounts without duplicate plans. A financial revision alone does not prove an emergency surge or establish responders' workload.

agricultural_groundwater_withdrawal.method: Keep water-use sector, area, period and the total behind any percentage clear. Distinguish measured from estimated withdrawals and dependence. Do not assign a whole-region depletion estimate to one sector.
agricultural_groundwater_withdrawal.uncertainty: Metering, underground boundaries, returned water and replenishment estimates vary. Water use or reliance on wells alone does not prove depletion or shortage.
agricultural_groundwater_withdrawal.boundary: Missing inventories do not prove excessive pumping. Do not combine unlike underground reserves into one balance or describe dependence as an actual shortage.

municipal_groundwater_withdrawal.method: Keep water-use sector, area, period and the total behind any percentage clear. Distinguish measured from estimated withdrawals and dependence. Do not assign a whole-region depletion estimate to one sector.
municipal_groundwater_withdrawal.uncertainty: Metering, underground boundaries, returned water and replenishment estimates vary. Water use or reliance on wells alone does not prove depletion or shortage.
municipal_groundwater_withdrawal.boundary: Missing inventories do not prove excessive pumping. Do not combine unlike underground reserves into one balance or describe dependence as an actual shortage.

industrial_groundwater_withdrawal.method: Keep water-use sector, area, period and the total behind any percentage clear. Distinguish measured from estimated withdrawals and dependence. Do not assign a whole-region depletion estimate to one sector.
industrial_groundwater_withdrawal.uncertainty: Metering, underground boundaries, returned water and replenishment estimates vary. Water use or reliance on wells alone does not prove depletion or shortage.
industrial_groundwater_withdrawal.boundary: Missing inventories do not prove excessive pumping. Do not combine unlike underground reserves into one balance or describe dependence as an actual shortage.

agricultural_nitrogen_application.method: Keep fertiliser type, organic additions, crop, treated area and application timing clear. Identify whether use was measured or estimated.
agricultural_nitrogen_application.uncertainty: Farm reports, crop areas, timing and organic inputs can be incomplete or inconsistent.
agricultural_nitrogen_application.boundary: Fertiliser produced or sold is not necessarily the amount applied to fields.

anaerobic_manure_lagoon_operation.method: Record animal species, manure added, liquid volume, temperature and storage time. Keep agitation, covers and treatment conditions clear.
anaerobic_manure_lagoon_operation.uncertainty: Manure composition, loading records and time held in storage vary between facilities.
anaerobic_manure_lagoon_operation.boundary: Regional livestock numbers do not prove that a particular manure lagoon is operating.

cattle_stocking_density.method: Keep animal type, usable grazing area, time interval and records of animals moving between paddocks.
cattle_stocking_density.uncertainty: Animal weight and the area actually available for grazing can vary.
cattle_stocking_density.boundary: Regional herd totals cannot replace paddock-level measurements.

coal_power_sulfur_emissions.method: Keep the power unit, fuel sulfur, pollution controls and operating hours clear. Distinguish measured emissions from estimates.
coal_power_sulfur_emissions.uncertainty: Assumed emission rates and the effectiveness of controls vary by generating unit.
coal_power_sulfur_emissions.boundary: Electricity generated alone does not establish sulfur dioxide emissions.

agricultural_soil_compaction.method: Keep soil moisture, texture, depth, management history and measuring method with the result.
agricultural_soil_compaction.uncertainty: Naturally dense soil layers can look like compression caused by farming.
agricultural_soil_compaction.boundary: Use soil measurements or a clearly limited assessment before labelling the ground compacted.

urban_hydrologic_supply_shortfall.method: Keep the water-service level, year, population and urban or rural coverage. Distinguish availability and water quality rather than merging them into a single cause.
urban_hydrologic_supply_shortfall.uncertainty: Country estimates and the aspects of water service measured differ.
urban_hydrologic_supply_shortfall.boundary: A global service gap does not prove that a particular utility rationed water or suffered a source shortage or treatment failure.

urban_water_demand_peak.method: Keep weather, population, customer types and available supply capacity with the peak-demand reading.
urban_water_demand_peak.uncertainty: A peak may last only a short time and may not represent ordinary demand.
urban_water_demand_peak.boundary: Total yearly demand is not a measure of pressure during the busiest hours.

urban_distribution_water_loss.method: Keep physical leaks and apparent losses together unless a checked water balance separates them. Apparent losses include water delivered but not correctly measured or billed.
urban_distribution_water_loss.uncertainty: Meter errors, unauthorised use, authorised unbilled use and physical leaks all affect water that generates no revenue.
urban_distribution_water_loss.boundary: Not all unbilled water is physically leaking from pipes.

urban_source_water_treatment_constraint.method: Record the year and the type of water service. Keep separate records of whether water is available when needed, whether people can reach it, and whether it is safe.
urban_source_water_treatment_constraint.uncertainty: The global gap combines problems with sources, pipes, availability and quality.
urban_source_water_treatment_constraint.boundary: Do not assign every service gap to insufficient treatment capacity or poor raw-water quality.

wildfire_smoke_pm25_exposure.method: Keep the monitor or satellite-model method, how population exposure is weighted and how smoke is separated from other pollution.
wildfire_smoke_pm25_exposure.uncertainty: Identifying the wildfire share and how much outdoor smoke enters buildings adds uncertainty.
wildfire_smoke_pm25_exposure.boundary: Total fine-particle pollution is not automatically wildfire smoke. Evidence separating the source is needed.

wildfire_smoke_exposure_duration.method: Keep the exposure threshold, missing periods, evidence linking smoke to fires and the event definition clear.
wildfire_smoke_exposure_duration.uncertainty: The length of a smoke event does not show how much each person breathed.
wildfire_smoke_exposure_duration.boundary: A fire's mapped boundary alone does not establish how long a community was exposed to smoke.

surface_water_inflow_deficit.method: Identify the waterbody, incoming water source, period and reference level. Keep the total used in percentages and whether gauges or models supplied the values.
surface_water_inflow_deficit.uncertainty: Basin boundaries, reference periods, satellite coverage and estimates of unmeasured inflows affect results.
surface_water_inflow_deficit.boundary: Regional rainfall alone does not prove storage loss. Unassessed basins must not be classified as unaffected.

surface_water_evaporative_loss.method: Keep the waterbody's area, measuring method, weather and time interval with the estimate of water lost to evaporation.
surface_water_evaporative_loss.uncertainty: Changing water levels affect surface area, and different methods can estimate different losses.
surface_water_evaporative_loss.boundary: Hot weather alone is not a measured amount of evaporation.

surface_water_groundwater_exchange_shift.method: Keep the difference in water pressure between surface and underground stores, local sediments, measuring or modelling method and period.
surface_water_groundwater_exchange_shift.uncertainty: Exchange varies over short distances and is difficult to observe directly.
surface_water_groundwater_exchange_shift.boundary: Nearby well readings alone do not establish which way water is moving.

surface_water_withdrawal_pressure.method: Keep the permitted amount, actual water taken, returned water, waterbody and reporting period separate.
surface_water_withdrawal_pressure.uncertainty: Withdrawal reports may omit when water was taken or how much returned.
surface_water_withdrawal_pressure.boundary: Permission to take water does not prove that the permitted amount was actually withdrawn.

coal_power_co2_output.boundary: A global indicator does not establish a local cause or exposure without evidence connecting it to that place.
